h1: The 6 Best Anti-Glare Privacy Screens for Monitors in 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 anti-glare monitor privacy screens from 21.5 to 34 inches, scored on fit, clarity, blue light filtering and value per screen.
summary: The SightPro 27 Inch filter is the best anti-glare privacy screen for most desks, with a standard 16:9 fit and a single-sheet design that keeps things simple. The SightPro 24 Inch is the pick for the most common monitor size, the Mamol 34 Inch handles curved ultrawides with blue light filtering, and the 21.5 Inch filter is the cheap way to try a privacy screen for the first time.
intro: The costliest mistake with a privacy filter is ordering by a rough size. A filter cut for a 24 inch 16:9 monitor is not the same sheet as one for a 24 inch 16:10 display, and a few millimetres of mismatch means a gap at the edge where the whole point of the product leaks away. Before you worry about anti-glare coatings or blue light claims, the sheet has to match the exact panel you own.

This ranking covers six filters across 21.5, 24, 27 and 34 inch screens, including two 2-packs and a curved-compatible ultrawide model. We reviewed the listings for aspect ratio, coating type, packaging and price bucket, and we judged each sheet on how likely it is to fit cleanly, how much it will dim your own picture, and what it offers for the money.

products.name: SightPro 27 Inch 16:9 Computer Privacy Screen Filter, Anti-Glare Protector
products.verdict: A plain, correctly sized 27 inch filter for the most popular desk monitor.
products.description:
The SightPro 27 Inch filter is a single sheet cut for 16:9 monitors, with an anti-glare surface and a privacy function that narrows the angle from which the screen can be read. Expect to pay $25 to $50.

It ranks first because 27 inches is the size where a privacy screen helps the most: the larger the panel, the more of it a neighbour can see from a side angle, and the more a glare-prone window behind you can wash it out. It beats the 24 inch SightPro only on that size logic, since both share the same formula and price bucket.

Buy it if you work in an open office, a shared home space or a cafe. The caveat is the usual one for privacy films: expect your own picture to look a touch dimmer than a bare screen, so you may need to raise the brightness.
products.idealFor: Open-office workers and shared-space users with a standard 27 inch monitor.

products.name: SightPro 24 Inch 16:9 Computer Privacy Screen Filter, Anti-Glare Protector
products.verdict: The same anti-glare filter for the monitor size most offices still use.
products.description:
The 24 inch SightPro is a single 16:9 sheet with an anti-glare coating, with the same coating as the 27 inch version, cut for the screen size that remains the default on office desks.

It comes second because the benefit of a privacy filter grows with screen size, and a 24 inch panel exposes a little less to side viewers. It also sits ahead of the 2-pack below, since a single sheet at this price is what most buyers actually need. The tradeoff is that you have one sheet only, so a dual-monitor desk means buying twice.

Choose it if you have one standard 24 inch screen at a desk with passers-by or bright windows. Check your monitor is truly 16:9 before ordering, as many 24 inch panels are 16:10.
products.idealFor: Single-monitor desks in offices or shared homes.
products.skipIf: You run two screens and want a bundle.

products.name: Mamol 34 Inch Curved Computer Privacy Screen Filter, Anti Glare Blue Light
products.verdict: Anti-glare, blue light filtering and anti-scratch in a curved-compatible 34 inch sheet.
products.description:
The Mamol is a 34 inch, 21:9 filter described as curved-compatible, with anti-glare treatment, blue light filtering and an anti-scratch surface. Expect to pay between $50 and $100.

It ranks third because the curved ultrawide is the hardest format to fit, and this is a sheet that explicitly addresses it. The blue light layer adds a warmer tint that some people like in the evening, and the scratch-resistant coating helps with a long panel that you wipe often. Against the SightPro filters it costs more and filters more of your own picture.

It makes sense for ultrawide users who need privacy across a very wide field of view. Expect a slightly warm colour shift, which matters if you do colour-critical work.
products.idealFor: Curved ultrawide owners who want privacy and evening comfort.
products.skipIf: You edit photos or video and need accurate colour.

products.name: [2 Pack] 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter, Anti Glare Blue Light
products.verdict: Two 24 inch filters with blue light filtering for a matched dual setup.
products.description:
This 2-pack supplies two 24 inch, 16:9 filters with anti-glare and blue light filtering, for between $50 and $100. That works out to a sensible per-sheet cost for anyone with a pair of identical monitors.

It ranks fourth because buying two matched sheets is the cleanest way to treat a dual-screen desk, and the blue light layer is a bonus. It sits below the Mamol because the Mamol serves a harder-to-fit format and adds scratch protection, and below the single SightPro filters because you only benefit if you really need two.

Buy it for a two-monitor home office. The caveat is the same colour warmth that any blue light filter adds, which can make whites look slightly yellow.
pros: Two sheets for a dual setup
cons: Wasted if you have one monitor
products.idealFor: Dual 24 inch monitor desks that want a matched look.
products.skipIf: You only have one screen or need true colour.

products.name: [2 Pack] 34 Inch Privacy Screen for Curved Monitor, Anti Blue Light Glare Shield
products.verdict: Two curved-compatible 34 inch sheets for a pair of ultrawides.
products.description:
This pack includes two 34 inch, 21:9 sheets that are curved-compatible, with an anti-glare treatment, and it costs between $100 and $200. It is aimed at the unusual buyer with two curved ultrawide monitors.

It ranks fifth because the audience is narrow, and the cost per sheet is higher than the Mamol if you only need one. Where it makes sense is a trading desk or a creative setup with two ultrawides, where a matched pair keeps the look consistent. The listing does not give coating detail beyond anti-glare, so we rank it below the Mamol, which spells out more.

Buy it if you have two curved 34 inch screens. Otherwise take the single Mamol sheet and spend the saving elsewhere.
products.idealFor: Desks running two curved 34 inch ultrawide monitors.
products.skipIf: You have a single ultrawide screen.

products.name: Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 21.5 Inch 16:9, Anti-Glare
products.verdict: A low-risk way to try a privacy filter on a small monitor.
products.description:
This is a single 21.5 inch, 16:9 filter with an anti-glare surface, and it costs $25 to $50. It targets the compact monitors that still fill many reception desks and secondary workstations.

It ranks last because it offers the fewest features and the least detail on the listing, with no stated brand history or extra coatings. It is still a decent trial buy: privacy filters are a personal taste, and some people dislike the dimming. Compared with the SightPro filters it simply has less behind it.

Buy it if you are testing the idea of a privacy screen on a small display. If you use the monitor all day, pay a little more for a filter from a clearer line like the SightPro.
cons: No blue light or scratch layer
products.idealFor: First-time buyers with a small 21.5 inch monitor.
products.skipIf: You want a filter you will use for years.

methodology.title: Size and aspect fit
methodology.description: We checked the listed size and aspect ratio on each filter, because a mismatch of even a few millimetres leaves a gap and defeats the privacy effect.

methodology.title: Anti-glare coating
methodology.description: Sheets that name an anti-glare surface scored for reflection control, and extra layers such as anti-scratch earned further credit.

methodology.title: Picture impact
methodology.description: Privacy films dim the screen and blue light layers tint it, so we weighed how much each filter is likely to change your own view.

methodology.title: Format coverage
methodology.description: Curved and ultrawide formats are harder to cover, so filters that address them directly gained points for that difficulty.

methodology.title: Value per screen
methodology.description: Price buckets were divided across the sheets in each pack, so the cost per monitor is what we compared.

whatMatters.detail: A filter is cut to a precise width and height, so it only fits panels of the same proportions. A 24 inch 16:9 monitor and a 24 inch 16:10 monitor need different sheets. Look up your monitor's resolution, and treat 1920 by 1080 as 16:9 and 1920 by 1200 as 16:10 before ordering.

A matte-textured face scatters light that would otherwise bounce straight into your eyes from windows and lamps. It cuts reflections but can add a faint grain to fine text. Check owner photos of the filter in use, and prefer a listing that names the anti-glare layer rather than only the privacy feature.

Privacy films work by blocking light that leaves the screen at wide angles, which is why your own picture also loses some brightness. Expect to raise the monitor brightness to compensate. Make sure the filter makes the screen unreadable from the side, and not merely tinted, before relying on it in public.

Most filters attach with adhesive strips, hanging tabs or slide-in clips, and the choice decides whether you can remove the sheet cleanly. Strips are neat but semi-permanent, while tabs let you take the filter off to share your screen. Read the listing for the mounting hardware and whether the bezel has room for it.

Blue light layers warm the picture, which many people find easier on the eyes at night. They also shift colour, so whites can lean yellow. If you edit photos or video, skip the tinted filters and rely on the monitor's own night mode instead.

howToChoose.subheading: Anti-Glare Only vs Anti-Glare Plus Blue Light

cards.label: Anti-glare only
cards.text: The SightPro 24 and 27 inch filters and the 21.5 inch sheet focus on reflections and privacy without tinting the picture. They keep colours closest to what the monitor produces.

cards.label: Anti-glare plus blue light
cards.text: The Mamol 34 Inch and the 24 inch 2-pack add a blue light layer that warms the screen for evening work. That helps comfort but moves whites toward yellow.

howToChoose.note: Pick anti-glare only if you care about accurate colour, and add the blue light layer if you mostly do text work late in the day.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: An exact size match, a clearly stated anti-glare coating and a mounting method that lets you remove the filter when you present. Check the filter against a colleague's view from the side before trusting it.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The SightPro 27 Inch and 24 Inch filters cover most office monitors with the simplest design. The Mamol 34 Inch suits ultrawide trading or design desks.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You run curved ultrawides or want the extra coatings. The Mamol 34 Inch and the 34 inch 2-pack are the only sheets here that handle that format.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have one standard monitor and want basic privacy. The SightPro 24 Inch or 21.5 Inch filter gets you there at the lowest price bucket.

faq.q: Will a privacy filter fit my curved monitor?
faq.a: Only if the sheet is labeled curved-compatible, like the Mamol 34 Inch and the 34 inch 2-pack. A flat filter on a curved panel tends to bow away from the edges. Check the monitor's size and curve before ordering.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake buying a privacy screen?
faq.a: Ordering the wrong aspect ratio. Many 24 inch monitors are 16:10, which makes a 16:9 sheet too short. Check your monitor's resolution, and compare the listed filter dimensions to your screen's width and height.

faq.q: Is a privacy filter worth it over just turning the screen?
faq.a: Yes for shared spaces. The filter makes side angles unreadable at all times, while turning the monitor is awkward and breaks your own posture. The tradeoff is a slightly dimmer picture on your side.

faq.q: How do I install a screen filter without bubbles?
faq.a: Clean the monitor and bezel, power it off and dry-fit the sheet first. Then attach the tabs or adhesive strips on the top edge and lower the filter slowly. Check the listing for whether it clips on or sticks.

faq.q: How do I clean an anti-glare filter?
faq.a: Use a dry microfibre cloth, and a barely damp one for stubborn marks. Avoid glass cleaner and alcohol sprays, which can strip the coating. The scratch-resistant Mamol is the easiest to wipe, but gentle pressure is still wise.

faq.q: Will the filter affect touch or webcam use?
faq.a: Touch screens may respond poorly through a sheet. A filter in front of a webcam on a laptop screen can also cloud the image. These sheets are meant for desktop monitors, so check where your camera sits.

finalTake: The SightPro 27 Inch is the easy pick for most desks, with the SightPro 24 Inch right behind it for smaller monitors. If you run curved ultrawides, the Mamol 34 Inch is the sheet that actually fits, and the 24 inch 2-pack covers a matched dual setup. Treat the 21.5 inch filter as a low-risk trial before you commit to a privacy screen long term.
